summary: Token duplication during fallback routing caused provisional overcharge and split invoice lines
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a ~24-hour provisional overcharge after a production incident where requests for their dedicated pool were transparently routed to hosted fallback. Impact: NimbleRetail observed a ~12% increase in token charges on their provisional invoice; charges split across multiple invoice lines (reserved and hosted) and one negative correction line appeared later. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-nyc-3), prod-us-east serving a high-throughput streaming chat workload. Steps to reproduce: 1) Simulate dedicated pool saturation by throttling two GPUs via load-shedding test harness in staging. 2) Trigger fallback policy to hosted pool (policy: latency-first). 3) Use the streaming chat API for a 2k token conversation and then finalize with non-stream aggregation. Observed behavior: Metering pipeline recorded both streaming deltas and the final non-stream token aggregation for the same request; when fallback occurred mid-stream, tokens were attributed to hosted at host rate and also kept under reserved accounting, creating double-counting. Expected behavior: Token usage should be de-duplicated and attributed to the final serving target; fallback should not cause parallel metering records. Logs & artifacts: referenced logs at s3://redwood-logs/support/SUP-550321/ and kube pod logs in #support Slack thread. Customer-provided timestamps and preliminary invoice excerpts attached in ticket attachments.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Aisha Patel (Support): Opened ticket after customer provided provisional invoice and sample request IDs. Asked for request IDs and timestamps for three sample sessions.

2026-03-10 | NimbleRetail - Ops (customer): Provided request_ids [req_f4a2, req_f4a3, req_f4b1] and attached provisional invoice PDF. Noted spike at 04:12 UTC when canary autoscaler triggered fallback.
2026-03-11 | Priya Malhotra (Billing): Observed split line items; provisional host charges present and a negative correction at 05:00 UTC. Marked as P1, escalating to SRE to verify dedup logic.

2026-03-11 | Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced streaming->non-stream duplicate records locally in staging when fallback happened at mid-stream. Created INT-4422 for internal patch work and opened metering PR.

2026-03-12 | Liam O'Connor (Support): Informed customer we will issue provisional credit equal to the duplicated amount and will backfill reconciler once hotfix merges. Asked for patience while we finalize timeline.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Fallback routing triggers two parallel accounting events: streaming delta meter and the non-stream final aggregation. The dedup key (session_id + request_seq) was not preserved across the host/reserved boundary, preventing deduplication.

Proof: Replayed problematic request IDs in staging with tracing enabled. Found entries in /var/log/metering/agg.log showing both STREAM_DELTA and FINAL_AGG for the same request id within 200ms across different backends.

Related code path: router/fallback.go and metering/aggregator.go. Root cause traced to token attribution middleware dropping the dedup token when switching to hosted path (middleware reset on HTTP redirect).

Risk assessment: High for customers that rely on streaming fallback; pattern occurs only when fallback happens mid-stream and when both streaming and final aggregation are enabled (common in chat + tools workflows).

Temporary mitigation considered: Disable streamed delta metering for requests that have fallback headers until dedup fix; however this has throttling/accuracy tradeoffs. Decided to apply accounting-side compensating credit first while deploying fix.
Monitoring: Added a Grafana query to highlight sessions with both STREAM_DELTA and FINAL_AGG within 1s across different backends (dashboard updated and linked in Confluence runbook).
resolution: Provisional actions: Issued a provisional credit of $1,384.72 to NimbleRetail's account (applied 2026-03-12). Engineering action: hotfix PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/891 merged to preserve dedup key across fallback routing and to deduplicate streaming deltas on final aggregation. Backfill: Billing pipeline run scheduled to reprocess 2026-03-09..2026-03-11 windows and apply adjustments to the finalized invoice; expected completion 2026-03-14. Follow-up: Postmortem draft assigned to Marco Ruiz; runbook updated with detection query and recommended temporary config change for autoscaler thresholds to reduce mid-stream fallback risk. Customer communication: Sent detailed summary and timeline; confirmed customer accepted provisional credit and requested postmortem. Ticket will be closed after backfill completes and customer confirms final invoice.
